item.description:

The Ministry of Transport’s failure is glaring in one key respect:

A National Passenger Analysis Center was established.

Every relevant ministry was supposed to authorize employees who could access the data and run relevant queries—for example, the Ministry of Health regarding passengers arriving from countries experiencing epidemics, or the Ministry of Transport regarding pilots from hostile countries.

The database was used, for example, to help locate the Israeli women who went missing in Vienna.

The Ministry of Transport never bothered to authorize any employees, never submitted a single query, and did not even bother to pay its share of the database’s costs.

If it was decided that pilots from hostile countries are not allowed to enter, how are you supposed to identify them if you haven’t even fulfilled your most basic responsibility—taking an interest and checking?

A real scandal.

A statement on behalf of the State Attorney’s Office:

The State Attorney’s Office recently filed an indictment with the Central District Court in Lod against a mathematics lecturer at Bar-Ilan University, a man in his approximately 60s from Petah Tikva, who, over a period of several years and motivated by nationalist-ideological considerations, conceived and planned to carry out an extreme and murderous scheme targeting hundreds of Arab Israeli citizens, including Bedouins, as well as Arabs residing in East Jerusalem and the Judea and Samaria area. The defendant called his plan “AYAT,” a Hebrew acronym for the words “The People Will Carry Out Transfer.”

The Central District Attorney’s Office charges the defendant with security offenses, including preparation to commit an act of terrorism under the Counter-Terrorism Law, extortion by threats, and obstruction of justice, and is asking the court to detain him until the conclusion of the legal proceedings against him. Please note that, pursuant to a court decision, a publication ban currently remains in effect regarding the defendant’s name.

According to the indictment, filed by attorneys Roy Reis and Tomer Steinberg of the Central District Attorney’s Office, against the backdrop of the “Guardian of the Walls” riots and, subsequently, with greater intensity against the backdrop of the “Swords of Iron” war, the defendant, motivated as stated by nationalist-ideological considerations, decided to plan and carry out numerous terrorist attacks simultaneously and cause the deaths of many hundreds of Arab Israeli citizens, including Bedouins, throughout the country, as well as Arabs residing in East Jerusalem and the West Bank. His objective was to cause them to flee and be permanently expelled to Jordan, Lebanon, and the Gaza Strip.

For more than three years, from the beginning of February 2023 until his arrest approximately two weeks ago, he conceived and prepared an organized, thorough, and detailed plan that he called “AYAT – The People Will Carry Out Transfer.” To implement and advance his plan, he undertook numerous concrete and varied preparatory actions, including preliminary reconnaissance trips, drafting documents setting out and detailing the proposed methods of operation and the justifications for them, and attempting to recruit participants for the planned terrorist attack.

Under the defendant’s plan, 72 Jewish terrorists, at least half of whom would hold firearms licenses, including the defendant himself, would be divided into 12 terrorist cells, with six participants in each cell. The participants would arm themselves with various weapons, including handguns, rifles, axes, and hammers, and launch mass terrorist attacks by complete surprise in mixed Jewish-Arab cities and Arab localities throughout Israel.

The plan further envisioned that the terrorist cells would receive assistance and backup, coordinated in advance, from subversive elements recruited from within the IDF, including the bombing of Arab population centers by the Israeli Air Force, Artillery Corps, and Armored Corps.

According to the indictment, in the practical section, which he titled “How to Carry Out AYAT Here and Now,” the defendant provided instructions for members of the public to join in “carrying out mass killing, rapidly taking control of friction zones, roads, entrances/exits to Arab communities, mixed cities and hospitals... to show no mercy even to their cruel and repulsive women and children, not to stop in the face of pleas, to harden hearts; any halt will lead to an intolerable state of chaos and then a massacre of Jews...”

According to the plan, the simultaneous mass terrorist attacks, together with amplifying and publicizing them on social media in real time, would cause all Arab citizens of Israel, including Bedouins, as well as Palestinians residing in East Jerusalem and the West Bank, to flee beyond the borders of the State of Israel. > >

To advance and implement his plan, the defendant spent approximately a year and a half attempting, unsuccessfully, to recruit supporters and partners. He also conducted preliminary reconnaissance around the locality of Tuba-Zangariyye in order to study and assess the best access routes and methods for attacking the community, which he intended to include as a principal target in the plan.

According to the clandestine recruitment framework he devised for recruiting participants to carry out the planned terrorist attacks with him, the defendant planned to approach Moshe Feiglin, who is running in the upcoming elections for the 26th Knesset as head of the Zehut party list and as number two on the joint Zehut–Religious Zionism list, recruit him into the plan, and subsequently use Feiglin’s assistance to recruit additional activists.

The defendant intended to invite activists who had been identified and selected in advance to a Zehut election event, where the invitees would be informed that they were being recruited for a terrorist attack in which they would participate the following day. The activists would be given a briefing document containing detailed operational orders and instructions for preparing for and carrying out the terrorist attacks.

The defendant attended two public events held by Feiglin and attempted to arrange a meeting with him and provide him with a summary of the plan, but Feiglin did not respond to any of his approaches.

Approximately one month ago, in view of the approaching election date, the defendant wrote an extortion letter addressed to Feiglin in which he criticized and insulted him over his failure to cooperate with the plan. He threatened that unless Feiglin promptly cooperated with him and assisted in advancing the plan, he would publicize the letter, thereby causing Feiglin, in the defendant’s view, reputational damage ahead of the elections.

Approximately two days later, the defendant went to Feiglin’s home and gave the extortion letter to a neighbor who happened to be passing by, asking her to deliver it to Feiglin, which she did. He subsequently attended a Zehut party event at Jerusalem’s Mahane Yehuda Market and, through another woman, delivered several copies of the extortion letter to the party’s director-general, together with an additional letter containing a threat similar to the one directed at Feiglin.

In the first half of the Trump administration’s term, the administration decided to close the world’s largest and wealthiest influence agency, USAID.

President Trump said that he really liked the agency’s “soft power” approach, but the problem was that the agency was plagued by a hard left-wing policy led by its senior officials, and therefore there was no choice but to shut it down.

Since the decision to close it was made, left-wing governments have fallen in the following countries, and pro-Trump right-wing governments (friendly to Israel) have come to power:

Ecuador – April 2025  
Bolivia – August 2025  
Honduras – November 2025  
Chile – December 2025  
Costa Rica – Feb. 2026  
Peru – June 2026  
Colombia – June 2026

And now Brazil is showing signs that it is heading for a similar shift.

At the beginning of Trump’s current term, I wrote quite a bit about USAID and its controversial activities, among them producing a “progressive” Sesame Street in Iraq, funding protests against various regimes, promoting a pro-LGBT agenda, and more.

It’s hard to believe there is no connection between dismantling the agency and the dramatic shift in South America. The agency had enormous budgets and decades of experience in the field. As mentioned, the largest and wealthiest influence agency in the world.

In Israel, we should welcome its closure. Many countries have joined the side that is friendly to Israel since it was shut down.

item.title: [amitseg] Brett McGurk, one of the Biden administration’s most senior officials, was interviewed on Dan Senor’s podcast (full disc
item.description:
Open
Brett McGurk, one of the Biden administration’s most senior officials, was interviewed on Dan Senor’s podcast (full disclosure, etc.) and rebutted a long list of claims and myths regarding the hostage deal. It is very much worth listening to, especially given that he served in an administration that clashed with Israel to the point of imposing an arms embargo.

Brett McGurk’s five main points about the negotiations to free the hostages:

1. “They could have brought everyone home almost immediately” — McGurk: absolute bullshit

According to him, a comprehensive deal in the early stages would effectively have required surrendering to Hamas’s terms, and even then there was no reason to assume Hamas would release everyone. The U.S. assessment was that Hamas intended to hold some of the hostages for years as bargaining chips.

2. The first deal collapsed because of Hamas — and the dispute was over the young women

McGurk says Hamas tried to move on to releasing older men while it was still holding young women alive. From Israel’s perspective, agreeing to skip over them could have amounted to a death sentence for those women. Israel therefore insisted on completing that category, and Hamas stopped the releases.

3. Before the Rafah operation, there was no deal that Hamas was prepared to accept

According to McGurk, Israel agreed to several very difficult proposals, including the release of prisoners convicted of serious offenses, and Hamas rejected them. Hamas also did not accept the Israeli proposal that Biden publicly announced. McGurk stresses that there was no point before Rafah when a deal was truly within reach. Moreover, Hamas would have waited years before releasing everyone.

4. Biden’s pressure to stop before Rafah was not because Israel had torpedoed a deal

According to McGurk, by that stage Biden had simply reached the limits of his tolerance for the war and the regional crisis. The U.S. pushed for a reduction in fighting during Ramadan—a move that McGurk says actually reduced Hamas’s incentive to compromise in the negotiations.

5. Sinwar and military pressure were the key

McGurk says that as long as Yahya Sinwar was alive, he saw no realistic possibility of a deal. This includes the killing of the six hostages, an episode that was portrayed here as the government having sacrificed them. The Rafah operation was part of the sequence of events that ultimately led to Sinwar’s killing, and according to McGurk, military pressure was what brought Hamas to the points at which it agreed to deals. In his view, military pressure and a hostage deal were not alternatives—the pressure was the leverage that made the deals possible.
